title: Anastasia's Mate
subtitle: Knight seals the escape, queen sac opens the h-file.
goals: Post the knight on e7 to seal g8 and g6
Deliver the rook mate on the h-file

steps.say: Named after the 1803 novel 'Anastasia und das Schachspiel', this is the most elegant of all h-file mates. The star is a knight on e7: from there it covers BOTH g8 and g6 — the king's front door and back door. With those sealed, a queen sacrifice on h7 drags the king into the open, and a rook arrives on the h-file to finish. Three pieces, perfect choreography.

steps.prompt: Warm up with the final picture: the queen has already given herself on h7 and the king took. One rook move ends it.
hints: The e7 knight seals g8 and g6; the g7 pawn blocks its own king. What's left?
Swing the rook to the h-file.

line.say: That's the picture: rook checks the file, knight owns both g-squares, the king's own pawn completes the coffin. Now let's build it from scratch.

steps.wrongSay: Every escape is pre-sealed — the rook just has to arrive. Which file?
steps.successSay: Finishing picture memorized. Now the full five-move choreography.

steps.prompt: The full Anastasia. Rook lifted to e3, queen on h5, knight ready. Five moves — begin with the knight!
hints: The knight must seal the king's escape squares BEFORE the sacrifice: which jump covers both g8 and g6?
Ne7+! Then give the whole queen on h7 — the king must take — and swing the rook to h3.

line.say: The seal. From e7 the knight controls g8 AND g6 — the king's only reply is the corner.
The queen gives herself to tear the king out of his shell — he MUST capture...
Anastasia's Mate. The rook checks down the h-file; g8 and g6 belong to the knight; g7 is the king's own pawn. A full queen invested, a full point collected.

rejections.say: The rook arrives before the doors are locked — Black just plays ...g6! hitting your queen, and the king breathes through g7. The KNIGHT seals first: Ne7+!
Kxh7 and the king strolls back via g6 or g8 — nothing was sealed! The knight check comes FIRST; the sacrifice only works against a king in a locked room.

steps.wrongSay: Lock the room, then burn it: knight seals, queen sacrifices, rook mates.
steps.successSay: Ne7+, Qxh7+!!, Rh3# — say it like a spell. You'll cast it in a real game someday.

steps.prompt: Now from the BLACK side — same pattern, mirrored. Your knight, your queen sac, your rook. Five moves to mate the white king!
hints: Mirror the choreography: which knight jump checks the king AND seals g1 plus g3?
Ne2+!, then Qxh2+!! forces Kxh2, and your rook slides to h6 for mate.

line.say: The seal, upside down: from e2 the knight owns g1 and g3.
The mirror sacrifice — White's king must take...
Anastasia in reverse. Patterns have no color: once the shape lives in your head, you'll execute it — and see it coming — from either side of the board.

rejections.say: Kxh2 and the king escapes via g1 — unsealed! Knight first, always: Ne2+ locks both dark squares before the queen invests herself.

steps.wrongSay: Same spell, other color: knight to e2 with check, queen sac on h2, rook to h6.
steps.successSay: Executed from both sides — Anastasia's Mate is now permanently yours.
